book.title: Behind the Mask of Innocence: Sex, Violence, Prejudice, Crime: Films of Social Conscience in the Silent Era
book.summary: "All the issues that torment America today were rampant in the silent-film era: crime, poverty, alcohol, drugs, racial and ethnic prejudice, epidemics, and the controversies over birth control, abortion, and the death penalty. And there were others that persist today but were then even more explosive: sexual mores, government and police corruption, prison conditions, immigration, and strife between capital and labor. Although many early moviemakers ignored harsh realities, choosing to depict a society shielded by a "mask of innocence," others went behind that façade, fighting the ever-present censors and producing films that made even the most sheltered moviegoer aware of deep rents in the country’s social fabric.

evidence: trade publisher signal: Knopf / Penguin Random House

argument.statement: Some silent-film makers challenged censorship and exposed social problems, making audiences aware of deep divisions in American society.

book.rationale: The book primarily explores the societal issues reflected in silent films, situating these discussions within the context of American cultural history.
